products.title: Rosho Classic Cashew Butter
products.short_description: Made in Tanzania. A story in every spoonful.
products.description:
Made in Tanzania. A story in every spoonful.

‘rosho began in a family kitchen in Tanzania in 2020. When the pandemic disrupted the founders’ cashew business, they turned a difficult moment into a new beginning, transforming their cashews into a smooth, creamy spread.

Named after korosho, the Swahili word for cashews, ‘rosho celebrates the ingredients and craftsmanship of its home country. Tanzanian cashews are roasted, milled, and packed locally, creating work for local women and keeping more value within the community.

Enjoy Classic Cashew Butter spread on toast, stirred into porridge, blended into smoothies, or drizzled over fresh fruit.

From a Tanzanian kitchen to your table, discover a delicious expression of East African creativity.

Net weight: 200 g.

products.short_description: Rare, distinctive, and beautifully bold, Africa’s Wildest is crafted with prized peaberry coffee beans, also known as “pearls.” Unlike typical coffee beans, peaberries develop as a single round bean inside the coffee cherry, creating their unique shape…
products.description:
Rare, distinctive, and beautifully bold, Africa’s Wildest is crafted with prized peaberry coffee beans, also known as “pearls.” Unlike typical coffee beans, peaberries develop as a single round bean inside the coffee cherry, creating their unique shape and sought-after roasting qualities.

Only about 8 to 10% of the coffee harvest produces these rare pearls, making every tin something special. The blend combines 80% Peaberry Arabica with 20% Robusta for an excellent cup with rich character and depth.

Blend: 80% Peaberry Arabica, 20% Robusta
Form: Whole bean
Size: 350 g tin
Sourced from: Tanzania

products.title: East African Bao Board
products.short_description: Gather around a game that has brought people together across East Africa for generations. Bao is one of the region’s oldest and most respected strategy games, traditionally played throughout Tanzania, Kenya, Zanzibar, and neighboring areas.
products.description:
Gather around a game that has brought people together across East Africa for generations. Bao is one of the region’s oldest and most respected strategy games, traditionally played throughout Tanzania, Kenya, Zanzibar, and neighboring areas. The Swahili word bao means “board,” and the game has long encouraged planning, patience, observation, and critical thinking.

Our board uses Bao 6×2, a recognized modern adaptation that brings the spirit and strategy of traditional Bao to a smaller, family-friendly format. Each set includes a 6×2 Bao board and 36 handcrafted East African bone beads, making the game as beautiful to display as it is engaging to play.

Designed for two players, the goal is to strategically sow and capture beads while thinking several moves ahead. It is easy to begin learning, but the possibilities grow as your strategy develops.

More than a board game, Bao is a connection to a tradition passed from one generation to the next. We hope this board finds its way into your own family game nights, friendly competitions, and traditions for years to come.

Includes: 1 Bao 6×2 board + 36 handcrafted East African bone beads
Players: 2

products.description:
A beautifully illustrated children's book inspired by the women, farmers, and communities of East Africa. Through Mary's journey, young readers discover resilience, hope, and how small changes can create lasting impact.

Mary is not just one girl.

She is many women.

Set in a small village in East Africa, The Mary: A Story of Light, Land, and the Women of East Africa follows a woman whose world begins to change as new opportunities bring light, education, and hope to her community.

Beautifully illustrated by Kenyan artist Benard Omondi, this inspiring children's book introduces readers to resilience, community, and the power of possibility. Inspired by real-world efforts supporting women farmers and rural communities across East Africa, The Mary connects farm to table and soil to soul through a story that encourages empathy, curiosity, and understanding.

Recommended for ages 5–9.
Written by Darci Dillin • Illustrated by Benard Omondi
